speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. I see you are a newborn presenting with respiratory distress; to begin my assessment, what was the gestational age at birth and were there any complications during delivery?

speaker: Patient
text: Newborn, born after the 32nd gestational week. The baby was born via cesarean delivery. The mother had gestational diabetes but was otherwise healthy with no other pregnancy-related diseases.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you. Given the preterm gestation (32 weeks), cesarean delivery, and maternal gestational diabetes, are you noticing any grunting, nasal flaring, or visible retractions in the infant? Also, have you observed any cyanosis or color changes?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Respiratory distress. I also have Tachypnea, Subcostal and intercostal retractions, Nasal flaring, Cyanosis.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Respiratory Distress Syndrome (RDS).

The clinical presentation of tachypnea, grunting (implied by distress in a 32-weeker), nasal flaring, retractions, and cyanosis in a preterm infant born via C-section is classic for RDS due to surfactant deficiency.

REQUEST TEST: Arterial_Blood_Gas_Analysis
REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray
